business_model.claim: Globalstar sells Mobile Satellite Services, meaning voice and data communications, to retail, business and governmental customers. It also sells wholesale satellite capacity.
quotes: including voice and data communications services to retail, business and governmental customers as well as wholesale satellite capacity services.

business_model.basis: stated in P3; figures from F2
business_model.claim: Revenue is reported in two categories: service revenue and subscriber equipment sales. In Q3 2026 service revenue was 65,386 and equipment sales were 5,517 (table in thousands).
quotes: Our revenue is categorized as service revenue and subscriber equipment sales.

business_model.claim: One wholesale customer, Apple, provided 64% of total revenue in the first nine months of 2026, against 63% a year earlier.
quotes: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, the Customer under the Updated Services Agreements was responsible for 64% and 63%, respectively, of our total revenue.

business_model.claim: Wholesale capacity services revenue was $44,603 in Q3 2026 versus $47,346 in Q3 2025. For the nine months it was $130,984 versus $126,440.
Apple pays a fixed service fee, fees tied to service-related operating expenses and capital expenditures, fees for expanded services, and potential bonus payments.
quotes: As consideration for the services provided by us to the Customer under the Updated Services Agreements, payments to us include a fixed service fee, fees relating to certain service-related operating expenses and capital expenditures, additional fees related to expanded services, and potential bonus payments subject to satisfaction of certain licensing, service and related criteria.

business_model.claim: A substantial portion of network operating costs is reimbursed by Apple and recognised as revenue. As a result, wholesale revenue moves partly with the timing and amount of reimbursed network costs.
quotes: In connection with services provided under the Updated Services Agreements, a substantial portion of these costs are reimbursed thereunder and such consideration is recognized as revenue in accordance with the terms of the Updated Services Agreements.

The majority of the increase during 2025 related to the timing and amount of service fees associated with the reimbursement of network-related costs as well as for fees related to certain expanded services.

business_model.claim: The company keeps 15% of its network capacity for its own subscribers and for other wholesale opportunities.
quotes: We retain 15% of our current and future network capacity to support our other customers, including our existing and future Commercial IoT, SPOT and Duplex subscribers.

business_model.claim: Subscriber services come from three lines: Commercial IoT, SPOT and Duplex. The company had approximately 806,000 MSS subscribers at September 30, 2026.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, we had approximately 806,000 MSS subscribers worldwide.

business_model.claim: Subscriber revenue is driven by average subscribers and monthly ARPU, which the company reports for each subscriber line.
quotes: ARPU measures service revenue per month divided by the average number of subscribers during that month.

business_model.basis: figures stated in P6; customer description from P1
business_model.claim: Commercial IoT grew in Q3 2026. Average subscribers rose to 591,114 from 542,715, monthly ARPU rose to $4.34 from $4.22, and service revenue rose to 7,694 from 6,867.
quotes: We provide Commercial IoT services to customers operating in a variety of industries, primarily government, transportation, construction, agriculture and forestry.

business_model.basis: figures stated in P6; explanation stated in P3
business_model.claim: SPOT declined in Q3 2026. Revenue fell to 8,594 from 9,452 and average subscribers fell to 202,952 from 220,609. The company attributes the subscriber decline to competitive pressure.
quotes: The decline in average subscribers is due to continued competitive pressure; however, product engineering efforts are underway to develop a new consumer SPOT device, which we believe could potentially increase demand for such services from our subscribers.

business_model.basis: stated in P3; figures from P6
business_model.claim: Duplex is shrinking because the company stopped making and selling Duplex devices. Q3 2026 Duplex revenue was 3,283 versus 4,726.
quotes: Duplex service revenue decreased $4.9 million in 2025 due to fewer average subscribers resulting from our decision to discontinue the manufacture and sale of Duplex devices to increase our focus on maximizing other sources of revenue.

competitive_position.claim: The first set of replacement satellites for the current network launched in August 2026 after delivery delays, and the second launch is scheduled for December 2026.

For example, as a result of delivery delays of the replacement satellites to support the Phase 2 Service Period, we were unable to timely launch the first set of replacement satellites that we are acquiring pursuant to the 2022 satellite procurement agreement with MDA Space.

competitive_position.claim: For its next-generation C-3 constellation, the company received a key FCC authorization and is expanding its ground network, expected to total about 90 new antennas at 35 ground stations in 25 countries.

This global expansion initiative is expected to include approximately 90 new antennas across 35 ground stations in 25 countries.

competitive_position.claim: Threat: the Customer can terminate the agreements at any time on advance notice, some fees are paid only if conditions are met, and the Customer may use other satellite providers.
quotes: The Updated Services Agreements impose a number of substantial obligations on us, provide for certain of our fees to be payable only upon satisfaction of the conditions therein and are terminable by the Customer at any time upon advance notice or force majeure event, or by either party upon the occurrence of certain events of default.

Further, the Updated Services Agreements do not prevent the Customer from allowing their devices to use another network provider's satellite services, which could also negatively impact our revenues that we currently expect to receive under the Updated Services Agreements.

competitive_position.claim: Threat: direct-to-cellular competition, including SpaceX's Starlink, which has partnered with a major US wireless carrier.
quotes: For instance, SpaceX has launched its Starlink constellation and has announced a partnership with a major U.S. wireless network operator to provide direct-to-cellular service.

competitive_position.claim: Threat: other satellite operators offer similar services, and the risk factors say many competitors have greater resources than Globalstar.
quotes: There are other MSS operators providing services similar to ours on a global or regional basis: Iridium, Thuraya, Viasat (through its acquisition of Inmarsat) and ORBCOMM Inc.
Many of these companies have greater resources, more name recognition and newer technologies than we do.

competitive_position.claim: Threat: terrestrial providers expanding into remote areas, and recent spectrum deals, may increase competition.
quotes: For example, recent spectrum transactions, such as between EchoStar and SpaceX and EchoStar and AT&T, may increase competition for our current and future products and services.

competitive_position.claim: Threat: second-generation satellites are not insured against in-orbit failure after their first six months, and one became inoperable in Q1 2025.
